**My reasoning, as this farmer:**

I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My family has about 8 mu of flat, irrigated cropland on the plain. My two children both work in the city now, so it's mostly me and my wife doing the work. I'm not going to experiment with anything new at my age — I grow what I know, what my neighbors grow, what the local seed station sells, and what the grain buyers will take.

This county runs on winter wheat and summer maize. That's the system. You plant wheat in October, harvest it in June, then immediately put in maize, harvest in September, and start again. Every mu I have goes into that rotation. I tried cotton once in the 1990s — too much labor, too risky. Never again.

For wheat, I'll use the improved semi-winter variety from the township seed station — probably 矮抗58 or whatever they're pushing this year. I apply base fertilizer before sowing (compound fertilizer) and topdress urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: once before winter sets in, once when it greens up in spring, and once when the grain is filling. Two sprays — herbicide in late winter, then aphid and powdery mildew spray before heading. Rotary tillage before sowing.

For maize after wheat, I use hybrid seed (郑单958 or similar). I spread fertilizer and work it in with rotary tillage, then plant. I irrigate if it's dry at sowing and again if there's drought during grain fill — but if we get good summer rains, maybe just once. Spray herbicide right after emergence, check for corn borer, spray once more if needed.

I expect about 450 jin per mu for wheat and around 1,100 jin for maize on a decent year. Not spectacular, but reliable.
